It seemed right at the time

Every case here is a real thing that was really built, and really broke. You get the reasoning that justified it — the honest, sensible case for the decision, written before anyone knew — and the parts that were genuinely correct. You do not get the bug.

Your job is to say where it broke. The three wrong answers are not invented: each is a real failure from a different project in the same domain. They are all things that have actually happened. Only one of them happened here.

Twelve cases. The deck watches which domains you misjudge and digs in there.

Drawn from 489 entries across 124 projects in a working engineering corpus — each with its own date, provenance and rule of thumb.
